There's also a lot of weird bugs, like only accepting the English pronunciation for Euro in the German speaking exercises. All of this is on top of an app that doesn't really teach any language very well (and some languages are embarrassingly bad). Duolingo is okay for learning some basics while using the toilet, but not very good for much else.

I've been using this app for 3 years next month and the ai aspect has made it harder and harder to use over that time. Now I have phrases that are PERMANENT stuck in my mistakes because "Falstaff" or whoever, refuses to accept my pronunciation of the words which I know I'm saying correctly! A lot of the time my oral exercises are marked wrong multiple times and I'm saying them exactly as the character does! VERY frustrating. I used to love this app.

Do learn Spanish here. Do not learn Korean here. Korean starts out great. You'll get a good tiny foundation, but section 2 tanks in quality. It no longer repeats vocabulary at you. You are expected to suddenly know new vocabulary you weren't taught which is worked around by tapping, but it feels messy. You're more worried about if you're reading it and pronouncing it right, if its new vocab or you just got vowels mixed up than what the focus is on. i.e. sentence structure, positive/negative

Duolingo is a really fun game style language learning app. But it's not perfect. I suggest getting a few other apps and juggling them I'm using it to improve my am Japanese. As I have a base, I don't know what the experience is for beginners. My biggest complaint about Duolingo is translating Japanese to English. I'll know exactly what it means, but there are too many words to arrange, it's worded funny,or it doesn't like the way I arranged words. There must be a better way to do this.

This app can be pretty fun in the beginning, but after a while, the lessons get very hard. Nothing gets explained to you which means you have to figure everything out for yourself. The stories and adventures are insufferable. Don't waste your money like I did on the premium subscription. I haven't used anything else, but I will be trying out Rosetta Stone soon. It's also extremely competitive if you want to move up in leagues.

New issue: The “practice to earn hearts” button is completely gone. A big loss to my learning routine. On major curriculum changes: Quality German learning content, as far as I can tell, but the newer “pathway” design actually makes me feel a little lost. I made fewer mistakes with the old castle style, even though the lessons I'd unlocked were at a higher difficulty than after the curriculum reboot. Even after using the new layout much longer, it's still not my favorite of the two.

After a year of having Super, I recently canceled it. I'm not interested in giving money to a company that uses AI for its content. That being said, the app is now unbearable. Not because of third-party ads, but because of Duolingo's own ads. There's an unskippable 30 second ad about Super after EVERY. SINGLE. LESSON.

I like using Dou on top of my other apps to study, usually. But lately I have been having difficulty with the speaking lessons. I'll frequently get questions wrong even though I said it correctly or the app will automatically select "I can't talk now" when mishearing my sentences. It's really discouraging. Sometimes I actually have to yell for the app to understand me which is beyond unhelpful and very annoying. It doesn't seem to be improving at all tbh.

free access is an absolute joke. God forbid you learn something new and mess it up. welp lost a heart. only get 5, which can go very quickly and suddenly one question from finishing a lesson and you lost all progress and have to wait until tomorrow to try again. The new energy mechanic is devastatingly awful, and it has immediately transformed a good app into something many people will abandon and forget. It's bound to alienate users via some classic, cynical greed. It's making the app unenjoyable and unusable. No one will bother with Duolingo if they can't finish their lessons or learn a single thing in the ad version. At least the heart system was based on performance. It was fair. Now, it's just a shameless paywall.

Duolingo has so many mistakes in the app that is infuriating, they show you the right answer but you the word is not even there,also when the work makes a sound but is the wrong spelling,when you are learning a language like Japanese everything matter,not just right or wrong,if you are trying to get to the next level on any language I recommend to get a real person that can actually explain. Duolingo will only give you the illusion that you are learning a new language

I really like the app. It's a great way to learn languages. But, PLEASE remove the Video Call Max upgrade as a main button. I already pay for the Super and have zero interest in spending the ridiculously high price for Max. I want the Practice Hub back as the default button. I was not happy about that Max stuff being pushed in my line of sight, but now I'm irritated that I need to select ellipses button to get to Practice Hub. Max should be there for those buying it. I am not going to.

Used the free version of this app for several years. It's ok if you don't mind that lessons are designed by Americans who are functionally illiterate in English (bad grammar, spelling, dumb local idioms). The app doesn't teach anything about the grammatical structures of your language of choice - you just fail by repetition until you progress. Then you get spammed by Temu and Duo ads. All I have learned is how to game the app to progress though. Learning foreign languages? Not so much.

A very extensive choice of languages to learn and each language's lessons are very long, offering learning for different learning levels. Overall it's good but there are annoying features. First, ADS. I don't remember using a free app that pushes their subscription as much as Duolingo. Secondly, the energy system is really counterproductive. It limits how many lessons I can do each day. Additionally, it doesn't make sense doing "Legendary" in any lesson. You're limiting my learning!

The app itself is really good, and the lessons are great for begining to learn a new language or keeping your skills up-to-date. My one issue is that after EVERY lesson, there is now a short advertisement followed by a longer advertisment for Max or Super Duolingo. I'm now resigned to doing one lesson a day as the repetitive advertisements is so annoying. Also, the phrase "Advertising helps fund Duolingo's mission" is a bit misleading -- advertising helps line your shareholders' pockets ;-)

EDIT: Removing 2 stars from my previous review. The app used to have hearts that remained as long as you got everything correct, now it's got this stupid energy system that runs out regardless of how much you get right. The amount of ads is genuinely ridiculous now. Often I have to click/wait through 3 or 4 ads. And now I've seen multiple ads for alcoholic beverages. Booze ads are the last thing I want to see in the morning, and for an "educational" platform I was surprised to see that they don't care what the ad content is. God forbid there are underage people or folks who struggle with alcohol abuse using this app.

I am hard of hearing...a hearing loss. I wear 2 hearing aids. There is NO accessible way to use this app. I struggle to understand what Jr & Zari are saying. Zari's voice is so high pitched & fast it doesn't register. Even when the turtle option is available I can't understand her. I don't have Super Duolingo anymore, I use the hearts. I basically lose hearts because I can't hear. Really?!!

This app is ridiculous. I regret actually paying for it. You pay for one version, and it doesn't even unlock all the perks that are actually helpful. They're always trying to get you to upgrade to a more expensive version. It's fun at first, but after a certain level, it feels more like a chore. The people in the higher leagues score so many so quickly that I'm not convinced they're real people. I went from finishing 1st place every week to not even being able to keep up with the leaders.

I am learning Spanish and doing better than I did in high school with a teacher. I can work at my own pace. It's kind of like a game, too, so it's lots of fun. The only thing I wish was if it explained things a little better from the beginning. As I advanced into the program, I got confused, but there are tips to help explain and all for free. Of course, there is the option to pay money for more help, better games (in Spanish or whatever language), and even calling videos. How fun.

I had had a 5 star review but there are some issues. Glitches with the music sections... I play the note and it remains greyed out. it thinks the note before was not- not sure... but have to restart the lesson. WHY?

What's going on recently ?? Many times I was granted a double/triple points for the next 10-15 min achieve the requirements and the same min disappeared. I want my double triple points back now !!!!! Also I am extremely irritated by the app. specifically after each lesson the flying monkey effect blows my head out

I use to love Duo but I now understand that for the conceptor IT'S A GAME NO A LEARNING TOOL I like the grammar rules but you can't learn be fluent unless you interact with somebody. at first i really love this app. it's cool i can learn a lot of languages, i can even learn math & music BUT the super/max ads this app gives everytime i finished learning is too much seriously. it's so annoying, give it but not everytime i finished. okay i know the super thing is cool like we can even do training, but NOT ALL ppl have it, so the ads is definitely too much. better if this ads thing is fixed to less ads, i hope u understand the ppl that don't have this super/max pack.

Does squashing those pesky bugs include unwanted and incorrect autocorrect? Excellent app. I would like to suggest allowing the user to select specific things to revise. I am learning Japanese and would like to revise the sentences more because the structure is so different. I cannot revise only the sentences at the moment. Other than a lack of targeted revision, this app is fantastic

Beginning levels are great for when you want to learn a little of the language of a country you are visiting, but after that I would not use this to learn a language from scratch. I use it everyday but only to supplement the formal classes I'm taking and to keep my vocab up now that I no longer live in the country I was learning the language for. You have to get Max in order to actually understand why you got a question wrong and there's no real explanation of grammar prior to doing a leason.

The "speak" exercise in your practice section sucks. I'm speaking the words but the microphone doesn't register what I am saying and keeps asking me to try again. FIX THIS ASAP. Next, for daily quests, stop forcing me to do "complete the next 3 lessons" or "read the next story in your path". It's ridiculous. Lastly, the app glitches out(awards I've earned keep disappearing, the layout for questions in lessons gets messed and words learned is at 0). I would give this app -10 stars.

This app used to be a great way to learn a language. You learn at your own pace-as much or as little as you like. Not anymore. The hearts system they used was perfectly fine but they changed it to the energy system-21 pieces of energy. Answer a question,1 piece gone,claim xp at the end of a round another piece gone. Really, Duolingo is that app for learning. I've been privileged to use a lot of learning apps, but Duolingo methods are really among the top tier, and they work. Simple things like streaks and the rewards really keep pushing. And the UI and total experience remains true to the app's policy of fun learning. Also really enjoying the new music and maths!

Dropped rating from five stars down to two because the lessons have gotten worse and have started making less sense. Yeah, you'll learn how to say things in the language you're learning and be able to communicate in basic terms, but that's it. I may be uninstalling soon because it's just not fun or interesting anymore.

Overall, this is an excellent app. I've been using the paid version to supplement my Spanish learning for months and will continue to use it. There are two changes I'd like to see: 1. I'd like to be able to download as many lessons as I want for offline learning. 2. I'd like to be able to opt out of leagues but still be able to track my friends' progress. As of now, it's both or neither. Once I see those changes, I will update my review to five stars because overall it's a great app!

I'm sad I had to go from 3 stars to 1. with the new Ai taking over and the abysmal state the app is in right now I'm going to delete it after this review. The app has so many bugs now its hard to do lessons. Some features aren't available anymore and the amount of gems it takes to do anything if frustrating when you earn them so few at a time. I'm very disappointed with how this app has changed and shame anyone who thinks this was a good idea.

It's pretty decent and a fun way to learn another language. However, you need to use it with something else if you want to make real progress. This is mainly because they removed the free tips, and they will no longer explain what you got wrong if you don't have the paid version. Unfortunately, that means all of us who won't fork out the extra cash or are just stumbling around in the dark now.

Pretty good for learning a language, breaks it down into manageable chunks. Sometimes it swamps you with new words when you could do with extra practice. The points system is broken. Sometimes says I'm earning triple, but only gives me 1.5x. Other times it says a lesson is worth 30 but only gives me 15. And the speaking element doesn't work properly. There's also an element of woke ideology, meaning it wants you to learn phrases that you won't need unless you're going on a woke holiday.

Absolutely love Duolingo - I've tried lots of other apps, YouTube etc, but it's just sticks with Duolingo! I've signed up to premium but you really don't need to! Learning with Duolingo feels a bit like a game, so I'm always trying to do better than the last round - it'll make sense when you use it! I started off just doing a lesson a day, now I do 5 or more every day - and I'm learning two languages fully, but dabbling with 4 others! Brilliant app - if I could give it more stars I would ⭐

My comments on the Lilly phone calls keeps saying something different from what I'm actually saying. It's extremely frustrating and is holding me back from engaging in an actual conversation. I wish they explained the usage of the words better. All of a sudden the usage of the words changes to a different spelling of the word and I don't know why. I seem to be googling the differences between words more than using your app. And google is free.

I am increasingly disappointed with Duolingo. It used to provide a clear series of lessons and encouraged me to practice my learnt vocabulary to recover lost hearts. This is no longer available. The inability to practice to recover lost hearts is motivating me to stop learning languages. I have tried the music lessons and I find the virtual keyboard lags and misses touches on my phone making it too difficult to get the one star to progress in the music playing lesson.

I really enjoyed this app when the voices were native speakers. Considered upgrading to a paid account until they switched over to ai and increased the subscription price. The AI voices often mispronounce words and do not help with learning to understand a native speaker. Still fun, but not as educational as it once was.

Before this, I would give 5 stars. I've been on duolingo since 2017 and it's gotten worse. The ads have recently become so obtrusive that the app is unusable. After each completed lesson, I must close the app and then reopen in order to progress any further. After completing over a six year streak, it's hard to say goodbye. But, the app is no longer fulfilling what it had promised.

After coming back after a few year hiatus, it's clear that the users are not the priority. There's no real incentive to keep learning past the multiplier timer. The push for AI content is atrocious and y'all should really be reading the room- nobody wants AI garbage. This used to be a really good app, but profit is clearly more important to you than your mission.

It's getting worse with ads since the last update. I do 15 mins of learning, I get 15-30 mins of ads. I could upgrade to Max,but why should I? I don't do streaming services like all the ads keep saying. Still struggling with audio sometimes, as I have been deaf from birth. Slowing speech down helps. But some words are misunderstood until I see them visually. I would still like to begin a language with alphabet, numbers & general phrases. Having a conversation with someone will be a huge test.

Big downgrade in quality within the last month. Numerous repeated lessons, weird glitches where a question doesn't appear and I have to close the lesson and start it from the beginning, and switching the voices of characters in discussions (very confusing when the man and woman's voices are switched- this has caused several mistakes for me). I wonder if the issues are due to Duolingo's transitioning to AI?

Engaging and rewarding in a game-like way. The notifications can be a bit much - quantity and aggression. Some things are oversimplified imo - lack of grammatical explanation, translating tense incorrectly, constant multiple choice instead of typing - but it's still educational. (This is based on my experience in Spanish and Japanese.) I don't like how you automatically follow people when you're "invited" to someone's Premium. You had me following opps. Add Tagalog / Filipino please!!

every time I think this game couldn't get any worse, it does. the new energy thing is stupid. I don't want to buy your stupid premium. if you gave me an option just to get rid of ads I would do it. but I like the fact that there's a risk of losing and having unlimited energy takes that away. you guys are really starting to suck.

I like the app! I'm doing Chinese on duolingo. I do 1 writing lesson & 1 regular lesson in the app each day. Each lesson takes about 5min. I always make sure I have 1 in each day and am on a 400 day streak. It's not as good as a full class with a real teacher to correct your pronounciation or writing, but its better than writing books and flash cards & audio is comparable to other audio lessons. If there were some chinese/taiwanese tv drama/video shorts that use the same conversations it'd help

It's pretty good for the most part. Something that is frustrating is the translations don't always line up. Glitchy.. still want areas of focus. Not good for kreyòl. Streak time is midnight, so if you are a late nighter, good luck. Worst- It doesn't teach. I've used duolingo for several years and have a 852 score streak. I enjoy using it, it's helped immerse me in my Greek heritage. But I don't think it's an effective teacher. daily user. I like it. not happy about the mass lay-offs. some courses are definitely better equipped than others. paying more for the AI tutor feature feels like a money grab. Amazing tool and good content for people interested in learning and exercising what they have learned. Now, regarding real feedback for developers: 1. Update2: Purposely making the UX for free users worse, Duolingo comes across as a cruddy company. Will probably give up soon. Update: worse still. Takes ages to load. Bugs. Original: The new interface/UX is unintuitive and time wasting in numerous ways.

I've had this for about 3 months now. I love the style of learning the language. I wish they would do something different for the listening in parts. It feels like you are made to fail because they have words you have not learned yet when they speak and then are asked to pick an option which I'll be honest, I get it wrong 50% of the time. If you don't have the super plan, you'll lose a heart for it.

My experience up until this point has been fantastic, I have enjoyed the scenes, fun practice made by other people for years with Duolingo. Learning that the board of this company decided to remove the human to human element that made Duolingo so personable and enjoyable in opt for AI was extremely saddening. I have been enjoying learning languages and now it will change, and people will lose their jobs and eventually Duolingo will fade away because they took away the human element.

I used to like it. This new "energy" system SUCKS. You can't do nearly as many lessons as under the hearts method. You just run out and there's no way to re-up... other than to pay. They really screwed up the experience with this. The enshitification of everything continues.

I like the app overall but there is definitely room for improvement. My biggest issue is, I wish there was on option to lower the volume of sound effects. I don't want to completely turn them off but it's really jarring because they're SO LOUD compared to the voices. I also wish the "practice weak skills" section would change more. It still seems stuck on the basic words I had trouble with in the beginning, even though I'm way beyond that point now. I can only translate "the" so many times.

I enjoy the app and think it is well done. It is a fun way to learn bits and pieces of a language. As someone who has studied languages before, it would be good to see a section with an actual explanation of grammar and rules. The only things I am not a fan of are the spoken exercises (they just doen't work on my phone so I always skpi them), and the dialogues (I think they are too complicated and have a lot of new words, at least in Mandarin, which make it very hard to get them right).

I accidentally purchased a year of Duolingo so decided to use it to learn chess. it was good at first, for maybe the first month, then I stopped improving. The exercises don't feel well designed and it feels like I'm doing the same easy ones over and over. The review, when matching against Oscar, seems very limited. I'd say it's ok if you are just starting out, but quickly stops teaching new things and doesn't pick up on your weaknesses.

It's a great app to be honest, but sometimes my sound doesn't work. Although, it does make up for that in solid lessons, helpful tips, and explanations for wrong questions. Thanks to this, I was able to learn, pronounce and memorize Hangeul (the Korean writing system) in less than half a year, plus a few Japanese characters. I would recommend this app to anyone who would like to start learning a new language from scratch or pick up from former lessons! Plus, Duo is so cute :)

Free version For a free app it's not bad. But you get 25 energy per day, and it doesn't get you far. If I'm going to pay for a language app, it won't be Duo. I'm doing German as a refresher, since I was conversational 30 years ago. I do notice some odd things, like the emphasis on the familiar rather than the formal pronouns. But a huge gripe is the flashcards, which pick up my answers only half the time, and then tell me my pronunciation is wrong, when I know it is not. Ruins my streak.

I really appreciate the effort people put into an app designed to help others. Yes, it's not the same to actually going to classes and learning a language that way, but it really helps to getting familiar with useful words and phrases, and if you actually keep using it, it helps at learning a new language quite fast, at least on a functional level. *Edit: I have no idea what's going on, maybe that they rely more on AI, but bugs are plentiful, app ignores achievements, marks mistakes erroneously

learning Spanish is so much easier than I thought! the only downside is that since I always practice at night, Duo always looks mad when I log on. If you have the time for more practice, by all means, buy it! If not, still use Duolingo. also, ads are minimal compared to other apps.

I'm learning, but something is wrong with the speaking exercises. The app incorrectly flags my pronunciation as wrong about half the time, even though I believe I'm saying the words correctly. My phone's keyboard, even when changed to French, autocorrects all the words to English so I have to type letter by letter, taking up half the time.

I am enjoying the Duolingo lessons for Ukrainian! The vocabulary review is good with a repeated exposure to the words. Then vocabulary is put together in short and longer sentences to promote sentence structure. If you make a mistake, you have the chance to review and correct it. The animations though silly, work to encourage you no matter what! What I would like to see as an option, is the ability to write words and sentences yourself. Writing helps to facilitate language use.

I used to have the premium account but deactivated it not too long ago since I have reached the maximum of Danish lessons (although it's still very basic). Having the non-premium account, I now have this energy bar which is really frustrating! If I make one - only one! - mistake in a lesson, my "energy" is not enough to finish it and I am forced to watch an ad or buy more energy. That is the opposite of motivating. I preferred the hearts which were more rewarding and logical.

Repetition on very easy words, then throws hard words in with little practice, then moves on bringing more words. So far, little teaching on the conjugation. After little instruction, you need to fill in Spanish words. I installed this app again, after uninstalling several times. Right now it won't let me go any further without paying or watching five ads. This has happened before. So I just don't practice for a day or two, and then it lets me carry on. Eventually I get annoyed and quit!

I HHHHHHAAAAATTTTTEEEE this app. It keeps pressuring you to practice every day, which I don't have time for. It also keeps bugging you when you get the answer wrong. It keeps bugging you to buy super. But super is Soo expensive. $100 JUST FOR Language lessons. Insane. Plus annoying. It shouldn't be #2 in learning. It shouldn't even be in the top charts. Useless. Don't download.

Pretty good app, but I wish the monthly challenges weren't always: complete 50 quests. Add some variety, like earn so much xp. And now I have to complete 70 quests, which is horrible, please keep it at 50, if you're not planning on adding variety. Also, there are a lot of bugs. when I completed a friends quest, I didn't get 5 quests added to the monthly challenge. Another bug being not getting any xp when I complete a chess game review. I would give 5 stars if it weren't for these things.

I might have given this app 3 or 4 stars at one point, but the quality has gone SO FAR downhill, the only reason I still use it, is because I HAVE learned a fair amount of Japanese from this app. Whatever AI they're using to make the lessons, went from okay-ish to probably the worst/cheapest they could find. When the lessons DO make sense, they're too easy, and when they don't, it's virtually impossible. Usually whenever I miss a question, it's because the hints and answers don't line up at all.

This is a great language learning tool! It has a lot of ways to challenge yourself and not get repetitive, there is even competitions! Of course, participating in said competitions isn't mandatory, if that's not your style. There really is options for everyone. It is free to use, although there are ads (as usual with free to use apps), with relatively cheap options to remove ads and boost learning if you feel it to be a worthy investment.

A decent starting place, and fair at teaching new vocabulary. But the app's primary goal is to keep you using it. If you want to understand grammar or learn to make practical use of the words you've drilled, Duolingo needs to be supplemented with other learning methods to be really effective. I do not have Duolingo Super. I accepted a one month free trial, thought I'd cancelled it successfully, and still got billed for a yearly subscription. I'll be more careful in the future.

Only been using it for 2 days. The way they introduce new vocabulary can be weird. They can take a while to define/translate new words for you. And they tend to translate phrases into equivalent phrases, not into literal words, which leaves out useful information. But it's pretty fun to use so far, and so I can't fault it as a tool to learn a new language, as the main factor will be time spent/engagement with the learning process.

Unusable for me, due to constant ads. I have used Duolingo before and decided to come back to it after a long break, but have uninstalled after less than 24 hours. There are long ads that can't be skipped after every single lesson which is ridiculous. I do not want or need anything other than the free version and constant ads will not change that. I'll look for an alternative.
